title: An AI-art game trailer, without generated in-between frames
author: CrownedGames
selftext:
I'm the developer of Pet The Damn Cat!, which uses AI-assisted art and audio. For this new cut, I wanted to show those assets inside the game rather than generate separate promo scenes.

The source captures are 20 fps. The export is 30 fps, but it repeats the captured frames instead of using AI interpolation. The seven gameplay sections run from petting and a faster shift through frenzy, a cucumber, a wrecking ball, adoption and the home. The UI stays in the frame, with the headline outside the playfield.

That keeps the original animation cadence rather than making it appear smoother than the capture. The footage is labeled full-game footage; it isn't a claim that every event or the adoption/home systems are in the demo.

For other devs using generated assets: do you keep the original captures for promotion, or interpolate them? If you interpolate, how do you separate presentation polish from movement a player will actually see?
